query: What documents are acceptable for NRI KYC video verification?
context: Section 4.2(a) of RBI Master Direction on KYC - For Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), overseas passport, valid Indian visa, and notarized overseas utility bill/work permit serve as Officially Valid Documents (OVDs). Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP) can be performed provided the geolocation check confirms overseas residency and live liveness detection is verified.
response: Under Section 4.2(a) of the RBI Master Direction on Know Your Customer (KYC), Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) may use the following as Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) for Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP): (1) Overseas passport, (2) Valid Indian visa, and (3) Notarized overseas utility bill or work permit. The V-CIP must confirm geolocation showing overseas residency and pass live liveness detection checks. Compliance Officers should ensure the V-CIP platform is RBI-approved and that all session recordings are archived per the bank's data retention policy. This matter should be reviewed by the Bank Internal Audit team and the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO).

query: Can a bank store transaction data in a public cloud outside India?
context: Section 8.1 of RBI Master Direction on IT Governance - All regulated entities (REs) storing banking transaction and account master data in commercial public cloud environments must ensure primary active and disaster recovery (DR) data residues remain within Indian geographical borders. Cloud service providers must be MeitY-empanelled.
response: Under Section 8.1 of the RBI Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, regulated entities (REs) are prohibited from storing primary active banking transaction data or account master data in cloud infrastructure outside Indian geographical borders. Both the primary and disaster recovery (DR) copies must reside within India. Furthermore, the cloud service provider must be MeitY-empanelled. Banks using Azure, AWS, or GCP must verify their selected regions are MeitY-compliant (e.g., Azure Central India region). Non-compliance may attract regulatory action under the IT Act and RBI supervisory review. This should be escalated to the CCO and IT Risk team for immediate verification.

query: What are the restrictions on outsourcing CISO functions to a third party?
context: Section 6.3 of RBI Master Direction on Outsourcing of IT Services - Regulated entities shall not outsource core management functions including Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) oversight, compliance auditing, and final credit approval. Third-party FinTech vendors must submit to regular SAS-70 or SOC-2 Type II audit inspections.
response: Under Section 6.3 of the RBI Master Direction on Outsourcing of Information Technology Services, regulated entities are explicitly prohibited from outsourcing the following core management functions: (1) Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) oversight responsibilities, (2) Compliance auditing, and (3) Final credit approval decisions. These must remain within the bank's direct organizational control. Any third-party FinTech vendors engaged for other IT services must undergo regular SAS-70 or SOC-2 Type II audit inspections. Banks should maintain an active vendor risk management program. This policy must be reviewed annually by the CCO and reported in the Board Risk Committee minutes.

query: Can a merchant store the 16-digit card PAN after payment authorization?
context: Section 5.4 of RBI Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls - No entity in the payment chain other than card issuers and card networks shall store actual card credentials (16-digit PAN, CVV, Expiry) after transaction authorization. All merchant checkouts must use RBI-approved Token Service Providers (TSPs).
response: Under Section 5.4 of the RBI Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls, merchants and payment aggregators are strictly prohibited from storing actual card credentials — including the 16-digit PAN, CVV, and card expiry date — after transaction authorization is complete. Only card issuers and card networks are permitted to retain this data. All merchant checkout integrations must migrate to card-on-file tokenization (CoFT) using an RBI-approved Token Service Provider (TSP). Non-compliance constitutes a serious breach of payment security norms and may result in suspension of payment processing licenses. The CCO and CTO should jointly audit all payment integrations to confirm full tokenization compliance.

query: What is the penalty if a bank issues an unsolicited credit card?
context: Section 6.1 of RBI Master Direction on Credit and Debit Card Issuance - Card-issuers are strictly prohibited from issuing unsolicited credit cards or upgrading existing cards without explicit written/digital consent. If an unsolicited card is issued or activated without consent and billed, the card-issuer must immediately cancel the card and pay a penalty of double the billed amount to the customer.
response: Under Section 6.1 of the RBI Master Direction on Credit Card and Debit Card Issuance, banks and card-issuers are strictly prohibited from issuing unsolicited credit cards without explicit customer consent. If an unsolicited card is issued and billed, the issuer is liable to pay a mandatory penalty equal to double the amount billed, cancel the card immediately, and reverse all charges without waiting for a formal customer complaint. This violation must be reported to the Board Consumer Protection Committee and reviewed by the CCO.

query: Can loan disbursements pass through a FinTech Lending Service Provider escrow account?
context: Section 4.1 of RBI Guidelines on Digital Lending - All loan disbursements and repayments must be executed directly between the bank account of the Regulated Entity (RE) and the bank account of the borrower. Under no circumstances shall loan disbursements or repayments pass through any pool, transit, or escrow account controlled by the Lending Service Provider (LSP).
response: Under Section 4.1 of the RBI Guidelines on Digital Lending, loan disbursements and repayments must flow strictly and directly between the bank account of the Regulated Entity (RE) and the bank account of the borrower. Passing funds through any transit, pool, or escrow account managed by a Lending Service Provider (LSP) or FinTech partner is strictly prohibited. Banks must ensure API integration connects directly with the core banking system. The CCO and Head of Digital Lending must audit LSP integration architectures.

query: What is the mandatory timeframe for reporting a major cybersecurity incident to RBI?
context: Section 11.4 of RBI Master Direction on IT Governance - Any major cybersecurity breach, ransomware infection, data leak, or unauthorized database access must be reported to the RBI Cyber Security and IT Risk (CSITE) Cell and CERT-In within 6 hours of detection.
response: Under Section 11.4 of the RBI Master Direction on Information Technology Governance and Cybersecurity, all regulated entities must report any major cybersecurity breach, ransomware attack, or unauthorized data access to the RBI Cyber Security and IT Risk (CSITE) Cell and CERT-In within 6 hours of detection. A detailed Root Cause Analysis (RCA) must subsequently be submitted within 21 calendar days. The CISO and Incident Response Team must maintain real-time SIEM escalation runbooks.

query: What are the Re-KYC periodic updation timelines for high risk vs low risk customers?
context: Section 38 of RBI Master Direction on KYC - Periodic updation of KYC (Re-KYC) must be carried out at least once every 2 years for high risk customers, once every 8 years for medium risk customers, and once every 10 years for low risk customers.
response: Under Section 38 of the RBI Master Direction on Know Your Customer (KYC), regulated entities must adhere to the following periodic Re-KYC updation intervals: (1) High-Risk Customers: At least once every 2 years with fresh OVD and address verification, (2) Medium-Risk Customers: At least once every 8 years, and (3) Low-Risk Customers: At least once every 10 years via digital self-declaration. Non-compliance may lead to operational account freezes. The Operations and Compliance teams must execute automated periodic refresh campaigns.

query: What is the mandatory cooling-off period for digital loans?
context: Section 7.1 of RBI Guidelines on Digital Lending - Borrowers must be provided a mandatory Cooling-Off / Look-up period (minimum 3 days for loans with tenor >= 7 days, and 1 day for loans with tenor < 7 days) during which they can exit the digital loan by paying the principal and proportionate APR without any prepayment penalty.
response: Under Section 7.1 of the RBI Guidelines on Digital Lending, regulated entities must provide borrowers with a mandatory look-up / cooling-off period of at least 3 days for loans with a tenor of 7 days or more (and 1 day for loans under 7 days). During this window, borrowers can exit the digital loan contract by repaying the principal amount and proportionate APR without any prepayment penalty or penalty fees. Digital lending apps (DLAs) must provide a direct in-app button for cooling-off exit.

query: Can a digital lending app access contact lists or media files on a borrower's phone?
context: Section 9.3 of RBI Guidelines on Digital Lending - Digital Lending Apps (DLAs) are strictly prohibited from accessing mobile device data including phone contact lists, media/photo galleries, and call logs. One-time access is permitted only for camera, microphone, and location solely for KYC and V-CIP onboarding with explicit consent.
response: Under Section 9.3 of the RBI Guidelines on Digital Lending, Digital Lending Apps (DLAs) and Lending Service Providers (LSPs) are explicitly prohibited from accessing mobile device contact lists, call logs, and photo/media galleries. The app may only request one-time access to camera, microphone, and location solely for completing KYC and V-CIP verification with explicit consent. Storing customer biometric data is strictly prohibited. The CISO and Compliance teams must conduct mobile app permission audits prior to app store release.
